                   ISNULL(UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(s.broker_code))), 'DIRECT') AS broker_code,

note: The products join compares the raw VARCHAR product_code values without any normalisation. Under the CI collation, case variants match; in Spark they would not, so policies would drop out of the inner join.
snippet: INNER JOIN stg.products p WITH (NOLOCK) ON p.product_code = s.product_code

note: The product_code join ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark needs an rtrim on both sides or padded codes miss the inner join.
snippet: INNER JOIN stg.products p WITH (NOLOCK) ON p.product_code = s.product_code

        INTO #gwp
        FROM stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
        INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = t.policy_id
        OUTER APPLY (

note: t.currency is CHAR(3) text, so currency = 'EUR' also matches 'eur'/'Eur' under the CI collation. A binary comparison in Spark would route those rows to the fx rate instead.
snippet: SUM(t.amount * CASE WHEN t.currency = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx.rate_to_eur END) AS gwp_eur

note: currency is CHAR(3) and the comparison ignores trailing spaces (e.g. 'EUR ' or a padded short code). Spark compares exactly.
snippet: SUM(t.amount * CASE WHEN t.currency = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx.rate_to_eur END) AS gwp_eur

note: amount DECIMAL(12,2) * rate DECIMAL(18,8), summed. The result's precision and scale must match legacy before the final rounding to 2dp.
snippet: SUM(t.amount * CASE WHEN t.currency = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx.rate_to_eur END) AS gwp_eur

note: OUTER APPLY TOP 1 picks the latest fx rate on or before txn_date and keeps transactions that have no rate. In Spark this must become a left join plus a row_number window.
snippet:
OUTER APPLY (
            SELECT TOP 1 f.rate_to_eur
            FROM stg.fx_rates f WITH (NOLOCK)
            WHERE f.currency = t.currency
              AND f.rate_date <= t.txn_date
            ORDER BY f.rate_date DESC, f._row_seq DESC
        ) fx

note: TOP 1 ordered by rate_date DESC, _row_seq DESC. The order is deterministic as long as _row_seq is unique per date, and the Spark window must use the same tie-break.
snippet:
SELECT TOP 1 f.rate_to_eur
            FROM stg.fx_rates f WITH (NOLOCK)
            WHERE f.currency = t.currency
              AND f.rate_date <= t.txn_date
            ORDER BY f.rate_date DESC, f._row_seq DESC

note: The fx lookup matches f.currency = t.currency, two text columns from different sources, case-insensitively. In Spark, case variants would find no rate and the premium would come out NULL.
snippet: WHERE f.currency = t.currency

note: The CHAR(3) currency match ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark matches exactly unless both sides are trimmed.
snippet: WHERE f.currency = t.currency

SELECT c.claim_id, p.broker_code, p.lob_code
        INTO #clm
        FROM stg.claims c WITH (NOLOCK)
        INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
        WHERE c.reported_date >= @YearStart
          AND c.reported_date <= @AsOfDate;

note: #keys temp table built by UNION, which removes duplicates; needs union plus distinct in Spark.
snippet:
SELECT broker_code, lob_code INTO #keys FROM #inforce
        UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #gwp
        UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #notified
        UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #paid;

        FROM #keys k

        LEFT JOIN…

note: DECIMAL(38,2)/DECIMAL(38,2) division is cut down to scale 6 in SQL Server and then rounded to DECIMAL(12,4), so the value is rounded twice. Spark's decimal division and cast must give the same ratio, which feeds the 0.75 flag.
snippet: CAST(SUM(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0)), 0) AS DECIMAL(12,4)) AS paid_to_written

note: The high-scale gwp sum is cast to DECIMAL(14,2), rounding half away from zero. Spark must cast the decimal and must not round a double.
snippet: CAST(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),

note: Claims paid is cast to DECIMAL(14,2). Spark must keep decimal types (not double) so the result matches.
snippet: CAST(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),

note: stg.brokers.broker_code is not normalised, but k.broker_code is upper-cased. The CI join still matches lower- or mixed-case broker codes; a binary Spark join would lose broker_name and status.
snippet: LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK) ON b.broker_code = k.broker_code

note: stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6), so it is padded with spaces and may also carry stored trailing spaces. SQL Server's join ignores them, while Spark needs rtrim on b.broker_code to match the trimmed key.
snippet: LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK) ON b.broker_code = k.broker_code
